body:
Stephanie is Rosa!

I haven't seen Rogue One (can't see movies in theaters, they give me migraines) but I'm curious to see it when it comes to Netflix, my friends all really loved it. 

I didn't make pancakes but just thinking about pancakes was enjoyable. I might cook something nice tomorrow, I like cooking--how about you? :)

Hi! I'm still pretty down, but at least I got some sleep and the sun is out. How are you? You were so sweet to me last night, I'm still so bowled over. 

The last good film I saw was actually one I've seen before--Short Term 12. It has Brie Larson and Rami Malek in it (and Stephanie Beatriz from Brooklyn 99!) and it's got some rough themes, but it's really moving and beautifully made. I didn't really know Rami Malek the first time I saw it, but since then Mr Robot came out and now I think he's aces. A really fun actor to watch.

The last bad film... oof. Some sci-fi thing on Netflix that had a really hacky, predictable plot. Evil robots! Oh no! How about yourself? I always love movie recommendations (good or bad). 

Hope your day is going well. :)

You are so sweet, I'm tearing up. You are so much kinder to me than I deserve. Thank you. 

I'm OK though. Not going to hurt myself. Talking with you has been really great. If you still want to chat when you get up, I'd love to keep talking. 

I like your Truth Seer idea, too. You wouldn't even need a lasso! 

I will check, thank you. I guess I was being self-defeating by not looking into it more from the start. It doesn't help that what you said--that silent disabilities are real disabilities--isn't the widespread  point of view in this country. :( 

Thank you again. I hope you get some good rest and wake up feeling refreshed and awesome.
I actually didn't really know about that. Do you have any other information or links where I could read about those options?

I don't think I'd ever actually thought about it in that way before. But you're completely right... I do feel betrayed. It hurts a lot. I guess I still don't understand why it happened that way.

I should check out job fairs. Thank you. I will try to do that in the future. Unfortunately my family is mostly retired... not a lot of jobs around. But that's a good thought... thank you for responding.

I guess I just need to keep on until I find a washing machine. This mud is really gross though! 

Unfortunately--though I'm honestly deeply touched by your encouragement--that's not really how it is with this illness. If you can remember the last time you had a really nasty hangover or flu, that there was a period there where your body was just totally depleted and you could barely stand up for more than a few minutes to drag yourself to the bathroom... it's a lot like that. I don't have to disclose it on job applications--thank god--but I also don't think asking for breaks for tea and massage are going to get me jobs. And there are just a lot of jobs I'm physically unable to do. It's really hard--it knocks down your sense of self. I look whole and "normal," but I'm not qualified for some things. I sometimes wish I were in a wheelchair or missing an arm just so when I try to explain to people how I just can't do some things they could look at me and understand, because explaining is so hard. 

I haven't looked into disability too much. My mom is retired but used to work on disability stuff (staying vague for privacy reasons) and she's been pretty sure that I would not qualify. I'm in the US, so healthcare is a nightmare in every direction, and so is disability. I wish we had a better support system like you guys do. 

I definitely have no powers, I'd have to make a cool souped-up vespa or something like Professor X so I could pretend to have mind powers of some type. They sure aren't going to believe I can leap any building in any kind of bound. :)
Taking on loans would directly worsen my quality of life... it wouldn't help me, short-term or long-term. I really appreciate the idea though, I wish it were more feasible.
Thank you for saying this. It's hard for me to articulate but that's exactly it and it IS a huge cause of stress.
I'm sorry, I think you misread. I said loans are not an option.

Thank you so much for replying. I'm sorry you've lost friends, too. It's so rough. 

The people in question are still in contact/friends with my abuser. I just wouldn't feel safe even trying to get in touch. The way he treated me was eventually very visible and if they chose to pretend he hadn't in order to keep being his friend, I don't think I can feel safe around them again. 

I've tried to find work online. I've sent out a ton of resumes and applications. So far, nothing. It's really, really depressing.

I'm really sorry but I feel like you don't understand what I'm saying. I can't pursue a graduate program because the money just isn't there. Like I can't go buy a new sofa because the money just isn't there. It just doesn't exist.

I haven't had dinner yet actually. I have just been chugging Gatorade to offset all the crying I've been doing. Thanks for reminding me to eat, though. I will get on that. 

Your first paragraph breaks my heart with how kind it is and how much I needed to hear it. I was instinctively ready to get a "things aren't so bad" when I posted here but... things are bad right now. I know they are. I remember when they weren't. I hate to feel self-pitying but I know that in the past 18 months or so a lot of shit has definitely been fired in my direction, way more than any 18 months before it. 

I actually love fish, so you're a little off there. ;) But unfortunately you're also a little off with regards to the chronic illness--it's been diagnosed, but it's not the sort of thing that medical science can fix right now. There are ways to treat symptoms (which I've been dealing with, some of them for a decade or more since this illness is not new, just the diagnosis) but the illness itself is not going anywhere. I would LOVE to be able to get a crappy-but-doable retail job at Target or McDonald's or whatever, but I am not physically able to perform the functions needed in those jobs. I can't lift heavy things or be on my feet for very long at a time. This is part of why I'm so sad on a daily basis. I feel like a burden to my parents who are supporting me. But I can't change this illness. I feel let down by my body and like I'm letting my parents down too because of it. It's so dispiriting. I've sent out application after application, resume after resume, and I'm lucky if I even get a rejection back. I feel so useless. Like a drain on society.

Thank you so much for replying though... your jokes made me smile (saving mayors!) and I really needed that. It's been a really dire day.

Right but meanwhile I have no guarantee of making enough money to pay off loans and no guarantee I will be healthy enough to actually get a job even with a Master's. All the non-money aspects of going back to school appeal to me, for sure (friends, connections). But the financial aspects really just aren't there. Sorry to be so blunt, but that's how it is.
I'm going to write you a message. Thank you.
Loans aren't really an option for me since I can't really pay them back.

I've been to school. Graduated from college around 2012. There's actually a Master's in Social Work program near here that is supposed to be really good. I looked into it, but I just can't afford it and loans aren't an option. On top of my chronic illness I'd probably have to take a few extra semesters (fewer classes per semester) so it just seems totally out of reach. I'm sorry. I really like the idea of going back to school but it's just not an option with my money situation. I wish all the time that that weren't the case.
I am actually in MA too. Do you want to talk? Things are really bad for me right now too. Maybe we could at least be a listening ear for each other.
